chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: 'By My Honour, My Majesty, My Magnificence, My Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My Position! No servant would prefer My desire over his own desire except that I would suffice him against his losses, and I would make the heavens and the earth guarantee his sustenance, and I would be for him behind the trade of every merchant.'
ai.seo_question: What is the divine promise for a servant who prioritizes God's will over their own desires?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, transmitted through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), highlights the spiritual principle of 'tadhyil al-nafs' (subduing the ego) by prioritizing divine will over personal desire. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted as a guarantee of 'kafa'ah' (sufficiency), where Allah becomes the ultimate backer of the servant's affairs, ensuring that their sustenance is secured regardless of worldly efforts. The imagery of God acting 'behind the trade of every merchant' underscores the metaphysical reality that true provision is divinely orchestrated rather than merely economically generated.

en.hubeali:
Al HHusayn Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washha, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Abu Ubeyda, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “By My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Honour and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Majesty, and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Magnificence, and My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Poisition! No servant would prefer My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Desires over his own desires except that I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would Suffice upon his losses, and the skies and the earth would guarantee his sustenance, and I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> would be Backing him in business with every businessman’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from ‘Asim ibn Humayd from abu ‘Ubaydah from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, says, ‘I swear by My Majesty, Glory, Greatness, Height and the height of My position, if anyone of My servant acts as I wish instead of acting according to his own wish, I will protect his lost and straying property and guarantee to provide him sustenance from the heavens and earth, and I will be for him (his supporter) in his business with every merchant.’”
